description: Convert between a nominal yearly rate (APR) and the effective annual rate (EAR, what a year of compounding really costs or earns), or find the rate hidden in a list of cash flows. Send compounding (annual, semiannual, quarterly, monthly, semimonthly, biweekly, weekly, daily = 365, or continuous) and ONE of: apr_percent (the nominal yearly rate), periodic_rate_percent (the rate for one period), or cash_flows (equally spaced amounts, the first at time 0, money received positive and money paid negative, such as [10000, -888.49, -888.49, ...]). Get back the rate per period, the APR (periodic rate x periods per year) and the EAR, which is (1 + periodic rate) ^ periods - 1 (continuous: e^APR - 1). For cash flows the periodic rate is the one that makes them net to zero. Answer fields: ok, verdict, result, rule, does_not, sources, observation, signature, verify. Errors: ok false with the reason (bad input, too large, hourly limit). Free. No model, no network, nothing you send is stored by the tool, and every answer is signed with LLPRO's key (check it at https://llpro.ai/effective-interest-rate). Not legal, tax or financial advice.

apr_percent.description: Nominal yearly rate in percent (12 for 12%).

cash_flows.description: Equally spaced cash flows, the first at time 0: received positive, paid negative. Exactly one change of sign (for example one loan amount in, then payments out). Up to 200.

compounding.description: How often the rate compounds or the cash flows fall: annual, semiannual, quarterly, monthly, semimonthly (24), biweekly (26), weekly (52), daily (365) or continuous (only with apr_percent).

periodic_rate_percent.description: The rate for one compounding period, in percent (1 for 1% a month).
